newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Anglian eyes international profits.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Anglian eyes international profits.

text.p: British water and sewerage firm Anglian Water plc expects to see operating profits from its international business in three to four years, John Green, managing director of the core water business said.
"It should be delivering operating profit by the year 2000, 2001," Green, who heads Anglian Water Services, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He said a review of international business under a new managing director appointed last July confirmed a strategy to focus on markets in North America, Panama and Australasia.
Green said Anglian also needed to ensure that its process engineering company Purac and fluid systems membrane firm in the U.S. "deliver profits."
Anglian took an 18.8 million provision in current results for its international business as it announced year pretax profits before exceptionals of 257 million stg, up from 238.6 million.
It also said it had agreed to take over Hartlepool Water for 19.5 million stg and cut bills for customers there by five percent from 2001.
Green said that cuts in overheads and accounting to contribute to cost savings and ease price cuts in its planned takeover of Hartlepool Water.
"We can take some overhead out...but the major cost savings will be things like taking out the cost of accounts, the auditing...and that sort of thing," he said.
Green said there had been no decision yet whether to move customer services under one roof but if a move was considered, the group would want to retain the local service in Hartlepool.

Green said the company, which operates in one of the driest areas in eastern England, was not expecting to have to curtail water use this summer, as the country endures its worst drought for 200 years.
"We expect to get through the summer without any restrictions," Green said.
